articleTitle: Metaverse as A Future of Education: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Learning has become the most important activity in our life. There are many ways to learn, but only some are interesting. However, by using technology, learning has become more exciting and attractive. One of the most promising technologies in education fields are Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality, which combines the real world with the virtual world. This virtual world is called "METAVERSE". With metaverse, we can interact with people in a virtual environment with life-like participants’ avatars. Some works of literature have used metaverse technology as a learning tool, making learning more attractive than seeing people on a screen. Through this research, we use systematic literature reviews to discover the possibilities, effectiveness, and advantages and disadvantages of learning using the metaverse. Based on our study, we can conclude that metaverse is proven to be an effective learning tool. Because learning in the metaverse gives many advantages, such as it helps to visualize materials and make learning more interactive, easier, and interesting for students, and also help teachers in the learning process. However, there are also some limitations, such as the cost of the device needed to support the metaverse. Therefore, there are more advantages to using the metaverse in education as a learning tool. Future development is needed to maximize the metaverse’s advantages and handle the limitations of the metaverse as a learning platform.

articleTitle: Prototype UX Design: Mobile Augmented Reality Application based on Gamification for Cultural Heritage Tourism
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: This study aims to identify the processes of UX designing a mobile application, Augmented Reality based on Gamification for Cultural Heritage Tourism, and to provide the prototype design and the testing result; this research employs the Design Thinking Method to design the prototype and uses the System Usability Scale (SUS) to identify and validate the testing result; the author establishes two research questions for this study, then explains the answers through a clear description of the stages of making a prototype which consists of the empathize, define, ideate, prototype, and testing stages, then to find out the testing results, the author uses the SUS method, scoring 88.5 in the excellent and acceptable categories; the originality of the research, this study provides the Design Thinking method to investigate the process of UX designing and the SUS Score method to calculate the resting result, helps build a complete understanding of developing the prototype and validation through testing comprehensively.

articleTitle: A Design of Childhood Stunting Assessment Feature with Agile UX Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: multidisciplinary collaboration between public health, system engineering, and UX is able to generate a solution in healthcare problem like stunting. The principle of Agile UX gathers requirements to generate an application design. Currently, various website and mobile applications are available to be utilized for stunting research. StuntingDB is one of many web-based applications that specialized in stunting data management. The application required several types of users to operate hierarchically. This research focused on Public Health Officers’ workflow that require a solution to in the form of assessment module for stunting DBMS by using Agile UX principle. The method collaborates agile team and UX team to solve Public Health Officer's difficulty in changing stunting status at pre-saved child patient's profile. Collaboration of both agile team and UX team successfully proposed an application design that system design.

articleTitle: Usability Evaluation on Life Insurance Application Using System Usability Scale and ISO 9241-11
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Many smartphone users make insurance companies race to provide services that make it easier for users to carry out their business activities. Still, many found that the mobile application lacks user experience and little research about usability in life insurance. Their rating value was as low as two to three stars from five in the Apps and Play store. The research aims to measure the usability evaluation of the one Life Insurance Mobile Application with a combination of SUS as quantitative measurement and ISO 9241-11 usability testing as qualitative measurement. This research resulted in an average effectiveness level of 76.3%, an average efficiency level of 77.62%, and a user satisfaction level of 67.04. This evaluation recommends improving the user interface design and user experience, especially the Help menu, since many life insurance users are not tech savvy and not in the usual condition (sick, trauma, etc.). This recommendation can be an opportunity for other life insurance industries to add new features to their mobile application.

articleTitle: Implementation of Agile Scrum Methodology in P4AI Application Development
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The profiling for Aptitude Inventory (P4AI) application is an application developed to help students carry out self-assessments so they can understand the interests of the appropriate majors and careers. The application was developed using the agile scrum methodology, which is a software engineering method that applies the principles of the AGILE approach so that it relies on the strength of team collaboration, incremental product, and iterative processes to realize the product with the best final result. The Scrum. The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether the scrum methodology applies to the requirements of application development. The results of the research are several outputs from the Agile Scrum Methodology process which is implemented in the development of the artificial intelligence based P4AI Application aptitude test website.

articleTitle: User Experience Evaluation of Kindteractive Application to Improve User Experience of Kindergarten Interior Introduction
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Technological advancements, such as the usage of augmented reality (AR) technology, are increasingly supporting the creation and implementation of more interactive learning media in the field of education. The conditions and scenario of the Covid-19 epidemic are also driving an increase in digital and online schooling. The more diverse the apps generated, the more they must analyze the user experience of the application’s design and operation. The User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) tool may be used to measure user experience in apps. With 26 questionnaire points, this test has six rating scales: attractiveness, perspicuity, efficiency, dependability, stimulation, and novelty. The UEQ Quality findings reveal that the Attractiveness scale is 2.04, the Pragmatic Quality scale is 1.68, and the Hedonic Quality scale is 1.17, all of which indicate good assessment results, implying that users prefer the program in terms of user experience. Users have utilized comparable programs based on this data, yet updates are still absent. Attractiveness, Perspicuity, Efficiency, and Stimulation are good scales. Based on the findings of the respondents’ data processing, it was determined that the application’s convenience was adequate in the user’s opinion. According to the statistics, the user loved the program.

articleTitle: New Narrative of Role Human-Computer Interaction in System Development
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Interaction between humans and computer is an interesting topic that studied in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI). HCI focuses on how humans can feel comfortable interacting with computers. HCI will help designers, analysts, and users to identify system requirements from text, fonts, layout, graphics, and colors. At the same time, HCI is usually connected with usability. Usability alone will confirm whether the system is efficient, secure, utility, easy to learn, remember, use, and evaluate. However, in its development, HCI is only limited to interface design and is used only at the design stage. Therefore, this study aims to learn and understand more about the importance of HCI and its usefulness in developing systems that will lead to user satisfaction. The main result of this research is to find out the importance of HCI implementation in system development. Moreover, this research also mentioned four types of HCI models or approaches that can be used in developing a system.

articleTitle: An Idea of Japanese Language Learning for Indonesians via Mobile Application Development
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Almost every aspect of the world has shifted online, including language learning. People's lifestyle of learning a new language has altered from traditional offline courses to learning a new language online. In learning the Japanese Language, it is a bit harder to learn it entirely online. This research used netnography and interview with the experts to get the insight about the Japanese language learning with the head of Japanese Language department from two universities in Indonesia. There are a lot of things that can be missed out, for example, making a mistake in pronouncing words or phrases and continuously making that mistake because there are no teachers to correct it, or learners lose motivation to keep learning. This paper proposed innovation to help solve that problem and create a more balanced way to learn the Japanese Language fully online.

articleTitle: "Ah-aloud": Method for Evaluating Cognitive Processes Occurring During Tasks from Vocal Information
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The think-aloud method, in which users verbalize thoughts generated during a task, provides insight into users' task-directed cognitive processes. However, verbalization during a task is burdensome and reactive, and the words used and amount of speech vary between users. To overcome this challenge, we propose the ah-aloud method in this study, wherein cognitive processes are expressed solely using "ah" and evaluated through vocal volume and intonation. Experiments compared to think-aloud using video game tasks with Japanese-speaking participants showed negligible difference in the reduction of verbalization burden and reactivity. It seems that people are very different regarding whether think-aloud or ah-aloud is easier. However, we found that ah-aloud can express various feelings, so we will establish ah-aloud position by comparing it with experimental methods to evaluate feelings, such as physiological signal measurement. We also discuss the recommended methods for obtaining think-aloud data. Additionally, we surveyed the literature pertaining to English interjections and discussed the possibility of extending this method to other languages.

articleTitle: Sasirangan Cloth Recognition and Shopping Experience Simulation Based on Virtual Reality Game with Non-Player Character Integration
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Sasirangan cloth is one of the traditional cloths owned by Indonesia and is a typical cloth originating from the province of South Kalimantan. This Sasirangan cloth has many motifs and is unique. Sasirangan cloth is also one of the potentials that can attract local and foreign tourists to visit South Kalimantan. However, in recent years, tourist visits to South Kalimantan have decreased due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. Then it also has an impact on the delay in the implementation of the Banjarmasin Sasirangan Festival which is usually held annually. The next impact is a decrease in turnover and interest in shopping for Sasirangan cloth, so that employees who work for Sasirangan cloth craftsmen are dismissed and reduce people's income. So the purpose of this study is to report the results of the development of a Virtual Reality Game application called VR-SasiranganKu by integrating the interaction of Non-Player Character (NPC) behavior with the type of narrative in the simulation genre game. VR-SasiranganKu is recommended to introduce and at the same time promote Sasirangan cloth to users, then justify the reaction to knowledge and shopping experience, and evaluate user experience using the UX Honeycomb method. Respondents involved as many as 100 people who are local and national tourists. The results show that the interaction of NPC behavior can provide good direction to users regarding the introduction of Sasirangan cloth by presenting an appropriate interaction design based on the narrative and the theme of the NPC that has been adopted, the results of justification using VR-SasiranganKu can provide knowledge reaction and very good shopping experience, and based on user experience evaluation that VR-SasiranganKu has adopted a very good UX with an average score of 4.91.

articleTitle: User Experience (UX): A Comparative Study Between Public and Private Institution Library Website In Indonesia and Malaysia
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The evolution of Internet is seen well progressed. From Internet 1.0 to now known as human intelligent. Every website will ensure their pages is suit and able to cater their users’ needs and functions. User Experience (UX) is one of the approaches that most developer will take into consideration when developing the website. It is crucial to measure the acceptance of the users’ so that improvement can be made. Apart from that, the users’ engagement is also seen important in ensuring the website is continuous use by the users. To students and researchers, library website is one of the most and common places they visited in completing their assignment, assessment and/or research. To get know the users experience in using their university library website, this study intended to measure to what extend their liking in using it. AttrakDiff questionnaire is used due to its effectiveness in measuring the UX. The study used 4 dimensions which are Pragmatic Quality (PQ), Hedonic—Identity Quality (HQ-I), Hedonic—Stimulation Quality (HQ-S), and Attractiveness (ATT). The study is using SPSS Version 26 to analyse the data and the results show that there are no significant differences among both local and private university in Malaysia and Indonesia. It is hope that the instrument of this study can be used as a checklist or assessment to web administrator to measure their website performance.

articleTitle: Integrating Good UX Development Practices in Solo Agile
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Background: Understanding customer needs with the collaboration of Agile and user collaboration has increased recently. Involving users in software development increases the value of the software product. User experience as an approach to solving user problems based on user subjectivity is able to further increase the value of the product. Moreover, startup products developed by an individual or limited team require added value to be able to compete in the market. However, lack of research articles that discuss the current issue and integration of Agile and UX. Aim: This study set out to answer the research questions. The first question is which development practices are suitable for managing UX in Solo Agile. The second question is what good practices for are integrating UX development in Solo Agile. And the last question is about which issues and challenges are associated with solo development with the user experience. Method: Systematic Mapping (SM) to represent the research trends and focus of the topic related to the field. Results: we retrieved one article from the 92 articles in the first iteration and 17 articles from the 308 articles from the second iteration. Conclusion: no article discusses the integration of solo agile and UX, however, there are few articles that talked the context of the UX that is related to the user-center design with solo agile.

articleTitle: Mobile Application for Augmented Shopping: Virtual Shoe Try-on and Virtual Equipment Placement
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The shopping experience has recently witnessed drastic changes with the ubiquity of online shopping, especially with the introduction of shopping through smartphones. The accessibility of these devices and their expanding functionalities have made them more popular in providing a full shopping experience. An obvious issue with common homeshopping applications is that customers cannot try the clothing items themselves. Also, when purchasing furniture or equipment that takes a significant amount of space, it is impossible to know if the item suits the room until it is already bought and delivered. Augmented reality can help customers to test whether the product matches what they are looking for. In this paper, we propose an augmented reality solution to enhance the online shopping experience. The proposed tool views the 3D equipment model using AR and sees if it fits in the identified space through the camera in the room. Also, users can try shoes through the cameras of their phones. Finally, a shoe size recommendation system is developed using a machine learning algorithm that detects the foot and returns the recommended shoe size. The application was evaluated on 10 users. The results show the effectiveness and efficiency of the developed solution. A set of four tasks are utilized to evaluate the solution in terms of the System Usability Scale (SUS) and task completion time. The research outcome can be used to help in developing a better user experience for a wider range of AR shopping applications.

articleTitle: User Usability Evaluation of E-Tourism Website in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Indonesia has been named the country with the most beautiful natural scenery in the world. This is an attraction for tourists visiting Indonesia. But in general, before a tourist visits a country, tourists will look for information on the website. Indonesia has an e-tourism website that tourists can visit, namely Wonderful Indonesia, which has the website address indonesia.travel. The problem that arises from this research is how the user experience of using this e-tourism website so that tourists get the experience of seeing the website. The method used is to use user usability to see how the tourist experience is made to be felt on the e-tourism website. The research approach uses quantitative and qualitative methods. The research question in this study is what factors can make the experience interesting for touristsƒ The result of this research is that the design structure is a significant factor, in addition to the fact that based on the interviews conducted, users tell what the experience is like when visiting the e-tourism website. The conclusion of this research is based on the needs, methods, and results state that e-tourism websites in Indonesia must always be structured and scheduled to analyze how the needs and desires of information design are needed by users. Especially must update the design structure that adapts to the variables that have been proven to be a benchmark for user comfort. because the design structure is the most important aspect in the user usability of an E-Tourism Website.

articleTitle: A Study of Smart Home User Personas Based on Context Theory
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: To achieve a safe, convenient, comfortable, and environmentally friendly home life experience, smart home field has reached a new stage of development, where actively providing user-centered service is crucial. Therefore, it needs to capture the real needs of users in different contexts accurately. This study proposes a theoretical method and structural model of user personas construction in the field of smart home. Firstly, we analyze the current research on smart home, and review the connotation and characteristics, construction methods, advantages and disadvantages of user personas. Then, we explain context theory and propose a method to build smart home user personas by combining context theory. The smart home product terminals and platforms collect and analyze user data in different contexts, and obtain contextual information including user, environment, time, and task, which are the elements of user behavior patterns and living habits to build a dynamically updated user persona with rich contents. This user personas model can be used in smart home platforms to provide active services and personalized recommendations for users, as well as help Eco-chain product iteration and design decisions.

articleTitle: Can Sentiment Mining of Novice and Expert User Survey Feedback Enhance the Digital User Experience?
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: In recent years, sentiment mining has been used within politics and social media to understand the emotions and opinions that people have about society and different political groups to help bring change. However, in the user centered design process, a main component that helps bring change is the use of user feedback and there has been little research in terms of adopting sentiment mining to assist with this and the user experience of an application. This research paper implements the use of sentiment mining on user survey feedback from Jupyter Notebook and has identified different components of the user experience that caters for novice and expert users independently. Recommendations from this research will help Jupyter Notebook create a user experience that caters to novice and expert users and their workflow needs. This initial analysis has identified that sentiment mining provides important and subtle enhancements for user experience that other tools and techniques do not provide. Therefore, this is a worthwhile method of user experience assessment to foster to enhance a digital user experience.

articleTitle: Exploring Design Guidelines of Mobile Exergame for Older Adults
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Mobile devices, such as smartphones and tablets, offer a wealth of opportunities for older adults to stay connected and engaged with the world around them. One of the most exciting applications of mobile devices for older adults is mobile exergames. Mobile exergames can make exercise more fun for people of a certain age especially older adults, which may inspire them to participate in more physical activity. However, current mobile exergames are not designed for the gameplay experience of older adults or to meet their expectations, and design guidelines primarily target the younger population. Thus, the purpose of this study is to explore the design guidelines recommendation for designing mobile exergames for older adults using two main methodologies. First is the literature survey followed by the semi-structured interview. Database such as SCOPUS and Google Scholar were used to identify relevant articles in literature survey. A total of 20 articles were included in the final process of qualitative analysis. The interview was conducted in a series of separate sessions with 10 people aged 56 and older. After conducting a thematic analysis on the data, nine design principles were discovered. From these design principles, 20 design guidelines are derived, which provide valuable guidance for the development of the mobile exergame for older adults in general. The recommended design guidelines discovered in this study may be important considerations for game designers who aim to develop mobile exergames for the older adult populations.
